lines.text: Every AI helper you have used follows hidden instructions. Today you write your own.
Many chatbots are given instructions before you ever type.
They say what the bot is for and how it should behave.
You can write these instructions yourself, with no code.
Start with the purpose, for example helping Grade 7 students with maths homework by giving hints.
Then choose the personality: patient, cheerful, or full of energy like a cricket coach.
Rules say what the bot must always and never do.
Refusals say how it politely says no, like “I can’t give the full answer, but here is a hint.”
Test your bot with normal questions, tricky ones and off-topic ones.
Write what should happen, then check what really happened.
If a test fails, fix the instructions and run all the tests again.
Here the learner pastes the instruction sheet as the very first message of a new chat.
It sets the purpose, the personality, the rules and how to refuse.
In this tricky test, the bot gave the full answer and broke its own rule.
That is why we test — we found a weak spot before a real user did.
We make the rule clearer, add an example of a polite refusal, and test again.
After the fix, the bot refuses politely and gives a helpful hint instead. Test passed!
You can test your bot by pasting the instruction sheet as the first message of a new chat.
Run each test, mark it pass or fail, fix the instructions, and test again.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
